source: Zdenek Vondrak, 'Konstrukcni navrh uhlove kyvadlove napravy' (Mechanical Design of Semi-Trailing Arm Suspension), Master's thesis, Brno University of Technology, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Institute of Automotive Engineering, 2013. Supervisor Ing. Petr Hejtmanek. Vehicle: Skoda 130 RS racing car rear axle.
figures: Thesis p.21 Tab.1 (left) and Tab.2 (right) point coordinates; p.28-30 ADAMS/View model description; p.30 Obr.23 toe and camber vs wheel travel (left axle, baseline); p.31 Obr.24 + Tab.4 toe for 9 pivot variants; p.32 Obr.25 + Tab.5 camber for 9 variants; p.22 wheel radius.
design_state: Measured points correspond to the unloaded, fully drooped wheel (maximum rebound). Travel 0 = this state; travel runs 0..120 mm in bump (damper stroke).
conventions: The published 'toe' and 'camber' (Obr.23) are the ADAMS body 3-2-1 yaw and roll + 90 deg of a wheel marker whose z axis is the spin axis and whose x axis is horizontal at the measured pose, not ISO toe and camber. Travel 0 = measured (fully drooped) pose, + bump.

camber_adams.how_read: 0 mm value from Tab.5 (0_0 min = -1.01); other values digitized by pixel analysis of Obr.23 (raster), uncertainty +-0.03 deg. SIGN: thesis states positive camber has negative values here, i.e. value>0 means negative camber (top inward). Endpoint at 120 mm: Tab.5 max = 1.83.

toe_adams.how_read: 0 mm value from Tab.4 (0_0 min = -0.47); others digitized from Obr.23, uncertainty +-0.02 deg. SIGN: negative = toe-in (agent check, see notes).

variant_min_max_tables_4_5.variant_naming: first value = shift of OUTER pivot forward/backward [mm], second = shift of INNER pivot up/down [mm]; direction sign not stated
variant_min_max_tables_4_5.variant_note: Variants were made by imposing a motion of the pivot point in the existing model, so the whole arm and wheel rotate rigidly about the other pivot; the variant curves start at different travel values (Obr.24/25). Tab.4 0_0 max toe 0.18 does not match Obr.23 end value 0.06 deg; the source does not explain this.

closed_form.method: Rigid rotation about the fixed pivot axis (instant axis = pivot axis; concept per Milliken & Milliken, Race Car Vehicle Dynamics, SAE 1995, Ch.17; page not verified). Let k = unit pivot axis, r = wheel point minus a point on the axis. First order: dz/dtheta = (k x r)_z; dcamber/dz = k_x/(k x r)_z; dtoe/dz = k_z/(k x r)_z; front-view swing-arm length = (k x r)_z/k_x = r_y - (k_y/k_x) r_x (lateral distance from wheel to where the pivot axis pierces the transverse plane through the wheel). Roll center: line from contact patch to that piercing point, intersected with the vehicle centerline.
